'''Shiomi-no-Sukune''' (''shiomi-no-sukune'', ''shibumi-no-sukune'', ''shionomi-no-sukune''<ref>"[https://sakaorinomiya.jp/s/top.html Sakaori-no-Miya Official Site]"</ref>) was a {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} and the first '''{{ill|Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|甲斐国造}}'''.

== Overview ==
The ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' and the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'' name {{ill|Sahohiko-no-Ōkimi|ja|狭穂彦王}} as the ancestor, and place him as kin of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|lt=Kusakabe-no-Muraji}}.

According to the tradition of {{ill|Sakaori-no-Miya|ja|酒折宮}}, when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} departed from Sakaori-no-Miya after visiting Kai Province, he said, "Let my spirit remain and rest here at the end of my journey," and gave a fire-striking pouch ({{lang|ja|火打嚢}}) to Shiomi-no-Sukune. Receiving the imperial command, Shiomi-no-Sukune enshrined the pouch as the divine object and built a shrine pavilion on the slope of Mount Tsukimi — this is said to be the origin of the shrine. The shrine's official history, along with {{ill|Isogai Masayoshi|ja|磯貝正義}} and {{ill|Hara Hidesaburō|ja|原秀三郎}}, identify the '''Mihotaki-no-Rōjin''' ("old man who tends the fire") appointed as eastern kuni no miyatsuko in the Sakaori-no-Miya tradition with Shiomi-no-Sukune.<ref name="#1">Hara Hidesaburō, "The Royal Authority and the Path Eastward," in ''Shinpan Kodai no Nihon 7: Chūbu'', {{ill|Kadokawa Shoten|ja|角川書店}}, 1993.</ref>

Shiomi-no-Sukune appears in the founding traditions of many historic shrines in Kai Province. For example: {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} is said to have originated when, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ja|景行天皇|lt=Emperor Keikō|lt_ja=景行朝}}, the deity {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|lt=Ōmiwa Myōjin}} was invited from {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|ja|大神神社}} in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}, and Shiomi-no-Sukune was installed as the founding priest. {{ill|Kanazakura Shrine|ja|金櫻神社}} is said to have originated when, in the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, Yamato Takeru visited on his return from the eastern expedition and ordered Shiomi-no-Sukune to build the shrine pavilion. {{ill|Kambe Shrine (Yamanashi)|ja|神部神社 (山梨市)|lt=Kambe Shrine}} is said to have originated when, during the reign of Emperor Keikō, Shiomi-no-Sukune brought the deity from {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡|lt=Mount Hiei}} in {{ill|Ōmi Province|ja|近江国}}. Nakamaki Shrine is said to have been founded when, in the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, Yamato Takeru — on his eastern expedition — issued the command at Sakaori-no-Miya to Shiomi-no-Sukune to found it on the central plain of Chinono-no-Oka in Yamanashi Kamigō.

Beyond shrine foundings, Shiomi-no-Sukune also appears in the discovery legend of {{ill|Shimobe Onsen|ja|下部温泉}}: while touring his territory, he is said to have stumbled upon hot springs and named them "Shiobe (Shimobe) no Yu," from which the origin of Shimobe Onsen is traced.<ref>"[https://www.spa.or.jp/kokumin/971/ Shimobe]," Japan Onsen Association.</ref>

At Kunitachi Shrine, the kuni no miyatsuko Shiomi-no-Sukune is enshrined as the deity.

== Genealogy ==
Son of Omi-no-Chitsuhiko-no-Kimi, third-generation descendant of {{ill|Sahohiko-no-Ōkimi|ja|狭穂彦王}}.
